name: OBR — published economic and behavioural effects of policy (AS2023–AB2025 packages, supply-side scorings, March 2026 decisions)

model.name: OBR policy scoring (demand multipliers + supply-side scorings)
model.method: Package demand effects via OBR fiscal multipliers; supply-side effects per measure via labour-supply elasticities (NICs, childcare, welfare conditionality), capital deepening (investment incentives, public investment) and TFP channels, scored against the pre-measures forecast baseline of each EFO round. Briefing Paper No.10 (Nov 2025) documents the framework and re-states every scored measure.
model.method_basis: EFO policy chapters/boxes AS2023-AB2025; OBR Briefing Paper No.10

baseline_key: Each row's counterfactual is that EFO round's pre-measures forecast; fiscal_event identifies the round. Not comparable across rounds without the baselines registry (#13).
period: Financial years 2023-24 to 2030-31 as published; briefing-paper supply-side impacts are single forecast-horizon numbers
coverage_note: Package GDP effects: AS2023 (by channel), SB2024 (by channel), AB2024 (by component AND by measure), AB2025 (by component). AB2025 CPI effects by measure. Per-measure supply-side impacts (percent of potential GDP, by channel) for every measure OBR has scored, SB2023-SS2025, from Briefing Paper No.10 Table 2.1. March 2026 total/direct/indirect effects of Government decisions on borrowing (nested, GBP). Counterpart compute (OBR emulator, PE-UK LSR, OG-UK) is issue #55 steps 2-3, not this build.
diagnosis_upstream: OBR scoring models are closed; divergence diagnoses classified as external-model issues become a comparison memo, not an upstream PR.
